name: Bologna Guglielmo Marconi Airport
before:
Bologna's airport, about 6 km north west of the city centre, and a practical arrival for the whole of Emilia-Romagna.

The monorail is the thing to use. The Marconi Express opened in 2020 and runs from the terminal to Bologna Centrale railway station in about seven and a half minutes, replacing the old Aerobus shuttle. From Centrale the rest of the region is a short train ride.

There are also daily direct buses to Ferrara, Florence, Modena, Ravenna, Rimini and Cervia, so a client can reach the Adriatic coast without changing in the city.

One practical note for a passenger with reduced mobility or a lot of luggage. There are no jetways at all here: all 24 departure gates are bus gates, so every boarding is by coach.

The terminal was expanded between 2011 and 2013 to 36,100 square metres. The single runway is 2,800 metres. The airport is named after Guglielmo Marconi, who was born in the city.
after:
Bologna's airport, about 6 km north west of the city centre and a practical arrival for the whole of Emilia-Romagna.

The monorail is the thing to use. Marconi Express trains run from the terminal to Bologna Centrale railway station in about seven minutes. From Centrale the rest of the region is a short train ride.

There are also direct buses to Ferrara, Florence, Modena and Rimini, so a client can reach the Adriatic coast without changing in the city.

One practical note for a passenger with reduced mobility. The airport lists only three boarding bridges for its 22 gates, and says wheelchair users board with a special vehicle or lift.

Its single runway is 2,800 metres. The airport is named after Guglielmo Marconi, who was born in the city.
